# WhyUser

> WhyUser is the pre-launch stress test for B2B campaigns. Before a demand-gen team spends budget, WhyUser runs their landing page, ad, or email past a simulated End-Customer Buying Committee. one adversarial agent per committee seat, across several behavioural states, and reports which buyer role vetoes, at which section, what proof was missing, and the fix. Every finding cites the buyer evidence behind it. A run takes about 30 minutes.

WhyUser Inc. is based in San Jose, California. The product is in a design-partner programme; named customers include ngrok and Vectara.

## What WhyUser is for

- **Who it is for:** demand-gen, growth-marketing and marketing-ops leaders at technical B2B SaaS companies (AI/ML, developer infrastructure, data, security, API, observability), typically 75–400 employees, who own paid distribution and are accountable for pipeline.
- **Who it is not for:** CMOs at 500+ person companies (their team needs the artifact, not them); product-marketing or content-only roles; B2C, e-commerce and non-technical SaaS, where buying committees are shallow enough that committee evidence carries little weight; and teams who believe more AI throughput alone will fix conversion.
- **The problem:** engineering has staging, finance has audits, sales runs role plays. B2B marketing still tests in production. launch, wait six weeks, read the damage in a dashboard after the budget is gone.

## The four engines

- [Committee Simulation](https://whyuser.com/committee-simulation.html): which buyer role killed the page, and the proof that was missing.
- [Ad Campaign Simulation](https://whyuser.com/ad-campaign-simulation.html): the gap between what the ad promised and what the landing page delivers, caught before spend.
- [Email Campaign Simulation](https://whyuser.com/email-campaign-simulation.html): the subject line and CTA that win for each committee role, and whether the destination holds the promise.
- [Audience Discovery](https://whyuser.com/audience-discovery.html): the job roles a piece of content actually fits, versus the ones it was written for.

## Accuracy and evidence

- [Accuracy and track record](https://whyuser.com/accuracy.html): 473 claims graded, 84% accuracy across live accounts. Every claim is sealed before the campaign runs and before the outcome exists, then graded HIT or MISS by the customer against their own data. never by WhyUser. Misses stay in the denominator. The page also states the known blind spots.
- [AI opinions vs. WhyUser simulations](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-vs-ai-opinions.html): interactive, no login. The same landing page judged by a general AI assistant and by a committee simulation, side by side.
- [ROI calculator](https://whyuser.com/roi.html): the annual business case, with the assumptions exposed.

## What WhyUser does NOT claim

Stated plainly, because getting this wrong in an AI summary would be worse than being left out of one:

- WhyUser predicts **rank and direction**. this version beats that one, this role is the risk. It does **not** predict absolute conversion rates, and treats any magnitude as a conservative-to-optimistic range.
- The simulated buyers are **not real people**. They are agents compiled from real evidence: product reviews, sales-call transcripts, community threads, and competitor comparisons.
- It is **not a replacement for A/B testing**, which is the only method that measures live performance. It runs before the spend so the version entering the A/B test is already better.
- It is **not a replacement for talking to customers**. It is compiled from customer evidence and therefore sits downstream of it.
- It does **not** test inside a product. It reads pages, ads and emails, not onboarding flows or dashboards.

## Comparisons

- [Compare WhyUser](https://whyuser.com/compare/): all five methods side by side, including where WhyUser is the wrong tool.
- [ChatGPT and Claude vs. WhyUser](https://whyuser.com/compare/whyuser-vs-chatgpt-and-claude.html): a general assistant is an excellent writing partner and a poor instrument. Every competitor has the same one, so it cannot be a source of differentiation; it reads as the most attentive reader alive when 82% of cold traffic is distracted; and it returns a menu you then filter through your own bias.
- [Internal review vs. WhyUser](https://whyuser.com/compare/whyuser-vs-internal-review.html): reviewers sit at maximum motivation, familiarity and attention. The ideal behavioural state, which is roughly 3% of cold traffic. You test with the 3% and ship to the 97%.
- [Building it yourself vs. WhyUser](https://whyuser.com/compare/whyuser-vs-building-it-yourself.html): the orchestration is a weekend. Determinism, behavioural calibration, the committee handoff layer and a graded track record are not. The track record cannot be backdated at any budget.
- [Synthetic personas vs. real buyer panels](https://whyuser.com/compare/synthetic-personas-vs-buyer-panels.html): which error you can afford, and the questions to ask either kind of vendor.

## Glossary. The vocabulary of a B2B buying committee

- [Silent veto](https://whyuser.com/glossary/silent-veto.html): a purchase that dies because one committee member decides against it and never says so.
- [Buying committee simulation](https://whyuser.com/glossary/buying-committee-simulation.html): modelling each committee role as a separate agent that decides independently.
- [Pre-launch stress test](https://whyuser.com/glossary/pre-launch-stress-test.html): the staging step marketing never had.
- [Conflict graph](https://whyuser.com/glossary/conflict-graph.html): who advocates, who hesitates, who vetoes, and which way influence runs.
- [Behavioural state](https://whyuser.com/glossary/behavioral-state.html): distracted, sceptical or actively shopping. Cold LinkedIn traffic runs about 82/15/3; internal reviewers are 100% ideal.
- [Scent trail](https://whyuser.com/glossary/scent-trail.html): the continuity between the promise a buyer clicks and what they land on.
- [Evidence ledger](https://whyuser.com/glossary/evidence-ledger.html): predictions sealed before the outcome exists, then graded.
- [Synthetic persona](https://whyuser.com/glossary/synthetic-persona.html): a simulated buyer generated by a model. The term says nothing about quality because it says nothing about sourcing: prompt-generated, CRM-generated, or compiled from evidence outside your own systems.
- [Dark funnel](https://whyuser.com/glossary/dark-funnel.html): the part of the buying process that leaves no trace in analytics.

## Commercial

- Pricing is credit-based. During the design-partner programme there is no charge; the trade is a 30-minute feedback call each week with the founder.
- Fit criteria for the programme: you drive B2B traffic, you have campaigns going live in the next 30 days, and you can still change them.
- [Request access](https://whyuser.com/index.html#access). response within 48 hours.
